raw_case_text: A 32-year-old man was diagnosed with diffuse large B cell lymphoma infiltrating the thorax wall with involvement of costal cartilages in August 2017. He was first treated with six cycles of R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine and prednisone) followed by four cycles of R-DHAP (rituximab, prednisone, cisplatin and cytarabine) without achieving remission. Surprisingly, disease restaging showed Burkitt lymphoma on chest biopsy, for which the patient was treated with an R Magrath regimen (R-IVAC: rituximab, ifosfamide, etoposide and cytarabine alternated with R-CODOX-M: cyclophosphamide, vincristine, doxorubicin and methotrexate) attaining complete remission. In September 2018, the patient underwent a stem cell transplant from a 10/10 human leukocyte antigen (HLA)-matched unrelated donor (MUD). Donor and recipient were both CMV immunoglobulin G (IgG) positive. The conditioning regimen consisted of thiotepa, busulfan and fludarabine. Graft-versus-host disease (GVHD) prophylaxis included cyclosporine, short course methotrexate and anti thymocyte globulin (2.5 mg/kg for 2 consecutive days). Fluconazole and acyclovir were given as antimicrobial prophylaxis. Neutrophil engraftment occurred on day +27 after transplant. During the first month after transplant, CMV DNAemia, tested two times per week, was around 1300-2000, below the threshold used to start therapy (3000 copies). On day +40, whole blood CMV DNA reached 37,000 UI/ml, and the patient was started on valganciclovir (VGCV) at 900 mg bid. However, after 9 days of therapy, DNAemia increased up to 1,46,800 UI/ml. Second line treatment with foscarnet 120 mg/kg was started promptly, leading to a slow decrease of viral load up to 25,800 UI/ml after 2 weeks of treatment (Figure 1). Following administration of steroids for the treatment of possible gut GVHD, a new flare of CMV DNAemia occurred on day +95. Genotypic resistance testing for the UL54 and UL97 genes was negative. The patient was treated with a combination of foscarnet 120mg/kg and VGCV 450 mg bid, resulting in the clearance of CMV DNAemia after 2 weeks of treatment (Figure 1). On day +160, the patient started complaining of conjunctival hyperaemia and a moderate decrease in visual acuity. Fundoscopy revealed papillary hyperaemia, retinal necrosis, haemorrhage and vasculitis consistent with CMVR (Figure 2), although whole blood CMV DNAemia was negative. Lymphocyte recovery was impaired significantly, with 69 CD4+ cells/mul, 221 CD8+ cells/mul and 82 CD19+ cells/mul. Aqueous humor biopsy showed presence of CMV infection (CMV DNA 230,400 UI/ml) while the presence of other viruses (herpes simplex virus, virus varicella zoster or Epstein Barr virus) was excluded; at the same time CMV serum DNAemia was negative. CMVR, once written informed consent had been obtained, was treated with foscarnet (180 mg i.v. and 1.2 mg intravitreal injection) combined with anti CMV immunoglobulin (cytomegatect) at 0.5 ml/kg every 2 weeks. After 4 weeks of systemic therapy, 20 weekly doses of intravitreal foscarnet and six cycles of immunoglobulins, a significant improvement in visual acuity was observed. The treatment was well tolerated with no side effects. Cyclosporine was tapered and then stopped on day + 315 (Figure 1). At 3 months after discontinuation of treatment, the patient started complaining of blurry vision. Diffuse atrophic chorioretinitis and posterior haemorrhage were observed. Retinal fluoroscopy demonstrated diffuse retinal vasculitis with loss of capillary, bilateral macular oedema, diffuse damage, vitreitis and steadily atrophic CMV lesions consistent with vasculitis requiring the administration of steroids at 1 mg/kg daily. Fundoscopic evaluation 2 weeks later was suggestive of reactivation of the viral infection given the presence of periangioitis and hyalinosis of the temporal area of the right retina. However, whole blood and humor aqueous CMV DNA were both negative. Maintenance therapy with VGCV at 450 mg bid was started during steroid treatment. After 4-6 weeks, visual acuity showed a moderate improvement, allowing a slow steroid taper. At 7 months after the diagnosis of CMV retinitis, the patient is in good general conditions and in continuous haematological remission (Figure 3).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 32-year-old male matched unrelated-donor allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipient (CMV D+/R+) presented on post-transplant day +160 with conjunctival hyperemia and moderately decreased visual acuity despite negative whole-blood CMV DNAemia.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Diagnosed in August 2017 with chest wall DLBCL/Burkitt lymphoma (achieving complete remission on R-Magrath [R-IVAC/R-CODOX-M] after failing R-CHOP and R-DHAP), the patient underwent 10/10 HLA-matched unrelated-donor allogeneic HSCT in September 2018 (CMV D+/R+; thiotepa/busulfan/fludarabine conditioning; cyclosporine, short-course methotrexate, and ATG GVHD prophylaxis; neutrophil engraftment day +27). Post-transplant blood CMV DNAemia flares on day +40 (37,000 rising to 146,800 IU/mL on valganciclovir) and day +95 (after steroids for suspected gut GVHD; negative UL97/UL54 resistance mutations) were cleared with intravenous foscarnet (120 mg/kg) plus valganciclovir (450 mg BID). On day +160, while whole-blood CMV DNA was negative, he developed conjunctival redness and decreased vision, and 3 months after completing ocular anti-CMV therapy developed recurrent blurry vision from immune-mediated retinal vasculitis.
subjective.past_medical_history: Thoracic wall Burkitt lymphoma / diffuse large B-cell lymphoma in complete remission status post R-CHOP, R-DHAP, R-Magrath, and 10/10 matched unrelated-donor allogeneic HSCT (September 2018; CMV D+/R+); recurrent post-transplant CMV viremia (days +40 and +95) and suspected intestinal GVHD.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for conjunctival hyperemia and decreased visual acuity on day +160, and recurrent blurred vision 3 months after stopping anti-CMV therapy.

objective.physical_examination: Day +160 ophthalmic exam: conjunctival hyperemia, moderate reduction in visual acuity, and fundoscopy showing papillary hyperemia, retinal necrosis, retinal hemorrhages, and retinal vasculitis. Follow-up exam 3 months after stopping therapy: diffuse atrophic chorioretinitis, posterior hemorrhage, vitreitis, bilateral macular edema, and temporal retinal periangiitis/hyalinosis OD.
objective.routine_investigations: Whole-blood CMV DNA PCR was 1,300-2,000 copies/mL in month 1, 37,000 IU/mL on day +40 (rising to 146,800 IU/mL after 9d of valganciclovir, then dropping to 25,800 IU/mL after 2w of foscarnet), flared on day +95 (cleared after 2w of foscarnet + valganciclovir), and was completely negative in blood at day +160 retinitis onset and during the 3-month post-treatment vasculitis flare.
objective.advanced_workup: Day +95 genotypic resistance testing for UL97 and UL54 mutations was negative. At day +160, lymphocyte subsets showed severe CD4+ T-cell depletion (CD4+ 69 cells/uL, CD8+ 221 cells/uL, CD19+ 82 cells/uL). Diagnostic anterior chamber aqueous humor tap on day +160 confirmed high-level intraocular CMV replication with a CMV DNA load of 230,400 IU/mL (negative for HSV, VZV, and EBV; repeat aqueous humor CMV PCR during the late retinal vasculitis flare was negative). Retinal fluorescein angiography during the late flare demonstrated diffuse retinal occlusive vasculitis with capillary nonperfusion, bilateral macular edema, and vitreitis.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of compartmentalized cytomegalovirus retinitis (CMVR) occurring in the absence of systemic viremia on day +160 post-allogeneic HSCT (confirmed by aqueous humor CMV DNA viral load of 230,400 IU/mL with concurrent negative serum CMV DNA PCR and CD4+ count of 69 cells/uL), followed 3 months after treatment cessation by PCR-negative immune-mediated retinal vasculitis/macular edema. CMVR was treated with 4 weeks of systemic IV foscarnet (180 mg/kg), 20 weekly intravitreal foscarnet injections (1.2 mg), and 6 biweekly infusions of anti-CMV hyperimmune globulin (Cytomegatect 0.5 mL/kg) alongside cyclosporine withdrawal (stopped day +315), resulting in marked visual acuity recovery. Subsequent CMV-negative retinal vasculitis responded over 4-6 weeks to oral prednisone (1 mg/kg/day tapered) under prophylactic oral valganciclovir (450 mg twice daily), with the patient remaining in continuous hematologic remission at 7 months post-CMVR diagnosis.
